case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
**Recommendation: if you fish the pier this week, go to St. Joseph. I'd still expect it to be below average. The other three ports look slow from the pier.**

**My ratings for pier salmon this week (0–4)**

| Port | Pier rating | Latest boat report (2023-07-26) |
|---|---|---|
| St. Joseph | 1 (below average) | 3, good |
| South Haven | 0 (slow) | 2, average |
| Grand Haven | 0 (slow) | Not rated |
| Muskegon | 0 (slow) | 2, average |

None of these ratings come from pier reports. The DNR reports I pulled for the last six weeks and for this time in earlier years list only boat anglers for salmon. The ratings are my inference from boat reports and water temperature.

**What the reports say** (newest report is 6 days old, from 2023-07-26)
- **St. Joseph** had the best report:
  - "Good success," and the most consistent water was around 120 feet (St. Joseph, 2023-07-26).
  - Spoons caught most of the fish. Rotators and flies also caught fish (St. Joseph, 2023-07-26).
  - "Some fish caught in 30 and 50 feet of water" (St. Joseph, 2023-07-26). That is the only sign of fish anywhere near shore.
- **South Haven** was average. The best water was around 110 feet, and rotators, flies and meat rigs worked best (South Haven, 2023-07-26). The week before, the catch was mostly lake trout with some coho and steelhead, rated 1 (South Haven, 2023-07-19).
- **Grand Haven** was a mix of salmon and trout in 80–140 feet of water. Salmon were 60–120 feet down on orange or green spoons and yellow or green meat rigs (Grand Haven, 2023-07-26). That report wasn't rated.
- **Muskegon** was fair, rated 2. The best action was 60–100 feet down in 90–150 feet of water, on green or glow spoons and green meat rigs (Muskegon, 2023-07-26). On 2023-07-19 it was rated 1, "hit or miss."
- **Water temperature (measured):** last week's average surface temperature was 75 F at St. Joseph, 74 F at South Haven and 72 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon. These were flat or slightly falling (+2, 0, −2 and −2 F over the week). Live conditions weren't available, so I have no pierhead temperatures, cold-layer depths or wind forecast.

**General guidance** (Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension, NY DEC)
- Chinook and coho prefer 52–58 F water. Warm surface water of 72–75 F is well above that, so salmon should be holding deep, which matches the 60–120 foot fish depths in the reports.
- Salmon come toward pierheads mainly during an upwelling, when north or east winds push warm water offshore and a sharp drop in surface temperature follows.

**My read**
- I'd expect no pier bite to speak of unless an upwelling happens. The reports show no upwelling this week, with surface temperatures steady and a little warm.
- I'd rank St. Joseph first because it had the strongest boat report and the only catches in 30–50 feet of water. A pier still reaches far shallower water than that.
- If a north or east wind of a day or more sets in and the temperature drops sharply, I'd expect pier chances to improve at all four ports. Check the wind forecast and nearshore temperature before you go.

**History** (same time of year, 2022)
- Early August 2022 was boat fishing in deep water. Chinook were 55–140 feet down in 120–250 feet of water at Grand Haven and Muskegon, and in 80–100+ feet at St. Joseph. South Haven was slow, rated 1 (reports dated 2022-08-03 and 2022-08-10).
- **Access issue, South Haven, 2022-08-10:** the piers were closed to fishing for several days because of red flag lake conditions. That was last year, but check the pier status if the wind is up.

**Caveats:** the reports are a week old and cover boats only. The wind forecast was unavailable.

- 2023-07-19: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/366250d
- 2022-08-10: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/327890a
